answerlines: The Tale of Genji (accept Genji Monogatari)

clues.text: In this novel, the Akashi Lady’s daughter gives birth to Niou, who romantically competes with Kaoru, the legal son of this novel’s title character.
The protagonist ‟s grandson, Niou, and his wife ‟s illegitimate son, Kaoru, pursue three sisters in the last third of this novel, after the title figure ‟s death.
This work's protagonist falls in love with Yugao, who is killed by the spirit of one of his mistresses.
A chapter between chapters 41 and 42 in this book is missing its contents and suggests the death of the titular character.
This novel’s protagonist is exiled to Suma after having an affair with his half-brother’s concubine, and “ Into the Clouds” in a blank chapter that signifies his death.

The title character was the second son of an emperor and a low-ranking concubine named Lady Kiritsubo and first marries Princess Aoi and later another girl who shares her name with the author of this work.
A friend of Tō no Chūjō raises Fujitsubo’s niece to be the perfect wife for the title “shining” Japanese prince in this novel.
The title husband of Lady Aoi seduces his stepmother Lady Fujitsubo in this novel.
Name this Heian-era novel by Murasaki Shikibu about the title “shining prince,” one of the world’s first novels.
Name this novel by Lady Murasaki Shikibu written during the Heian period in Japan.
One character in this work is exiled to Suma after his secret affair with his brother’s concubine is revealed, and that character’s mother dies when he reaches three years of age.
The protagonist of this novel compares the robe of one love interest to a cast-off cicada shell.
A character in this novel is possessed by a rival’s spirit after a conflict depicted in the “Battle of the Carriages.”
The title character of this novel is exiled to the town of Suma due to an affair with a concubine.

This novel’s Uji chapters, which focus on the rivalry between Kaoru (“COW-roo”) and Niou (“NEE-oo”), follow a blank chapter that is titled “Vanished into the Clouds,” which implies that the title character died.
The protagonist of this work has many love affairs, including with his step-mother Fujitsubo, much to the dismay of his wife Lady Aoi.
The main character of this work is presumed to have died in the chapter “Vanished into the Clouds.”
Both the Emperor Kiritsubo and the title character in this book are attracted to Lady Fujitsubo because of her resemblance to a concubine.
After marrying Lady Aoi, this work’s title “shining prince” has an affair with Lady Fujitsubo.
Name this early novel about a Heian noble written by Lady Murasaki.
In his study Seeds in the Heart, Donald Keene suggests that a chapter of this work was ordered destroyed since it told its readers to "flee the world."
This book’s protagonist builds a mansion with wings for each of the seasons and directions, which house his four most important lovers.
The protagonist of this book insults a female acquaintance by comparing her to a “broom tree” before doing the “Waves of the Blue Sea” dance.
This novel’s author appears in it as a preteen who is raped by the title character.
The story continues through such sections as “A Wreath of Cloud” and “The Bridge of Dreams” until the protagonist marries a girl he raised who shares her name with the author.
The death of one character in this work is signified by the blank chapter “Vanished Into the Clouds”.
A blank section called “Vanished into the Clouds” implies the death of this novel’s protagonist, a “shining prince” married to Lady Aoi (“ah-oh-ee”).
This novel's title character is called "Shining" and is unfaithful to his wife Lady Aoi.
The husband of Lady Aoi courts women such as Lady Utsusemi and Lady Fujitsubo in what magnum opus of Murasaki Shikibu?
Name this Japanese work written in the Heian Period, by Lady Murasaki.
